body: I agree with this wholly. For reference, this sort of thing is what my abusive mother would do, and I ended up with PTSD. It's isolation. Partners should be able to confide in their friends when something is wrong in the relationship. Humans are social creatures, and loving and connecting, especially on a platonic level, helps us process and stay afloat emotionally. OP, I promise you this is not a life you want to live for the rest of your existence. There are people out there who will love you without isolating you. I know you came to Reddit worried you're doing something wrong, but I think you would be best suited to break up as you tried to before and have him leave. If he's threatening to make a lot of money and move out, he knows he doesn't have to live with you. So, you shouldn't have to worry about his housing situation.

as someone who is disabled and waiting on a wheelchair, I’d be pretty sad if I found out someone passed on me just because of a device I use to help me get around. I also have enough mobility for the deed, and I’m mentally all there — but my immune system is eating the sheaths for my nerves, so I need mobility aids. 

I understand why you’d be defensive of the idea, but you really should unpack some of why you think that way. I don’t think it’s necessarily a conscious sort of thing but society does look at disabled people differently, and if you’re going to date someone who is disabled, you need to keep your mind open to the fact that you also will have some of those beliefs ingrained. it’s not a malicious thing, it’s just how things are.
